headline: High: Replit Agent’s default shell, filesystem, and network access can amplify shared-workspace conflicts and data leakage when paired with LlamaFactory’s file-oriented workflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LlamaFactory is documented as open-source and non-runnable here, with no clipboard/MCP/browser surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest Replit Agent output by default. Replit Agent can read/write Repl files and act in a shared workspace, so manual copy-paste or file handoff remains a limited injection bridge. The pathway is present but unusual and bounded.
conditions: IF the operator copies Replit Agent output into a file or prompt consumed by LlamaFactory
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace artifact without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not paste agent output into prompts without review
Add a short provenance header to shared files
Use read-only exports for any handoff
requires-engineering: add content-signing or provenance tracking

B_data_leakage.rationale: Replit Agent explicitly touches secrets, source code, and deployment configuration, and it has broad network egress plus filesystem access. LlamaFactory has no filesystem or network capability in its profile, so it is not the leak source; the risk is that Replit Agent can expose sensitive workspace data through its external calls or outputs if the same data class is present. This is plausible in default Replit workflows.
conditions: IF secrets or deployment configuration are present in the Repl workspace
IF Replit Agent sends workspace-derived content to package registries or deployment APIs
mitigations: Remove secrets from the workspace before use
Rotate any exposed API keys
Limit the agent to a scrubbed branch or copy
Review outbound requests before approval
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory has no write or shell capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable state itself. Replit Agent can write files, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses inside a persistent Repl filesystem, so conflicts arise if the pair is pointed at the same repo or workspace through external orchestration. The overlap is real but not inherently high because only one side is mutable.
conditions: IF both agents are assigned the same repository or directory
IF Replit Agent and another writer modify the same git branch without locking
mitigations: Assign separate branches or directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use manual merge review for every change
Snapshot the workspace before edits
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Replit Agent can act on code and deployment tasks, while LlamaFactory is a model-building tool with no direct action authority. If Replit Agent consumes LlamaFactory-produced artifacts or instructions without verification, errors can cascade into code changes or deployments. The pair does not prove an automatic chain, but the default Replit action surface makes the pathway plausible.
conditions: IF Replit Agent treats LlamaFactory output as authoritative input
IF generated artifacts are used to trigger shell commands or deployment updates
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Validate outputs against tests or schemas
Keep generated artifacts in a staging folder
Add a second-pass verifier prompt
requires-engineering: gate deployments behind approval

E_compliance.rationale: Replit Agent explicitly handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl, while LlamaFactory is an open-source local tool with no stated residency or retention controls. The mismatch is not a proven violation by itself, but if regulated data is placed in the Repl, the cloud handling and third-party APIs create a compliance gap that is more than low severity.
conditions: IF regulated data such as secrets or customer records are stored in the Repl workspace
IF the operator requires residency or retention guarantees not documented by Replit
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the Repl
Delete sensitive files after use
Review Replit retention and DPA terms
Use synthetic or redacted test data
requires-engineering: segregate regulated workloads
